the genome sequences of 10 different strains of the bacterium P. fluorescens were determined, and that comparative genomics of these genomes revealed that they are highly similar, and that they are more similar to each other than to any other bacteria.

the use of comparative genomics can help in the identification and characterization of bacteria, in the understanding of the evolution of bacterial species, and in the identification of the genetic characteristics of bacteria that can be used as biomarkers for the identification of bacteria.
the genome sequences of different species are useful for discovering characteristics that are unique to particular species and for elucidating the evolutionary history of different species.

the development of novel bioinformatics tools and approaches for comparative genomics, the application of these methods to the analysis of bacterial and viral genomes, and the use of the results to elucidate evolutionary relationships, identify novel genetic characteristics, and discover new tools for the identification and characterization of organisms.

the development of new reductive approaches to the analysis of genome sequences that can identify characteristics that are unique to different species and provide insights into evolutionary relationships.

the development and application of novel computational methods for the discovery of reliable genetic characteristics that can be used to elucidate the evolutionary history of different organisms and to provide novel means for the identification and characterization of bacteria, viruses, and other microorganisms.

genome sequencing has provided an unprecedented amount of data that can be used to reliably elucidate aspects of physiology, metabolism, and evolutionary relationships for a wide range of bacteria and viruses.

the genome sequences of many species are available today, and that the application of comparative genomics has already provided many insights into evolutionary processes, and that it will provide even more insights in the future.
genome sequences have the potential to reliably provide new and unique means for distinguishing different species and for understanding their phylogenetic relationships.
